seoTitle: How to Change a Microsoft Forms Name Easily (2026)
metaDescription: Learn how to rename a Microsoft Forms survey or quiz by editing the title directly inside the form editor without breaking your share link.
intro: Fixing a typo or updating a survey title in Microsoft Forms isn't done from the home dashboard grid, since the rename option lives inside the actual form editor rather than a right-click menu. This guide shows how to find your form from the dashboard, open it, click directly into the title field, and swap in a new name without breaking your existing share link or losing collected responses. It's a quick fix for anyone managing several active questionnaires who's clicked around the dashboard looking for a rename option that isn't there.

steps.heading: Find your form on the dashboard
steps.body: The Forms home page lists your work as tiles under tabs like Recent, My forms, and Filled forms, each one showing the form's name, its owner group, and how many responses it's collected so far. This is where most people instinctively look for a rename control first, since a right-click or three-dot menu is the usual place for that kind of edit in other apps.

image.caption: The Forms dashboard under the Recent tab, listing saved forms as tiles with their response counts — including the form we're about to rename.

steps.heading: Skip the dashboard's ellipsis menu
steps.body: Hovering a tile reveals a three-dot ellipsis menu, but it's worth knowing upfront that this menu is built for copying and moving forms between folders, not renaming them. Clicking around in it looking for a rename option is the most common dead end in this whole process, so the faster path is to just open the form itself instead.

steps.heading: Open the form and click its title
steps.body: Click the tile to open the full editor, where the form's name sits as a large text header right at the top of the canvas, above the question list. Click directly on that header text and it becomes an active, editable field with a blinking text cursor — no separate edit button or menu required, the title itself is the input.

image.caption: A form's title sitting in the editor as an active editable field, with the cursor placed and ready to type.

steps.heading: Clear the old title and type the new one
steps.body: With the cursor active in the title field, select and delete the existing text, then type the new name straight in. The field behaves like any plain text box — select-all and retype works fine if you're replacing the whole thing, or you can just fix a single misspelled word if that's all that's wrong.

image.caption: The title field cleared out mid-edit, ready for a new name to be typed in — the same click-to-edit behavior applies to every form.

steps.heading: Click away to save automatically
steps.body: There's no dedicated save button for the title change — press Enter, or simply click anywhere else on the white canvas, and the new name takes effect immediately. The editor's status indicator near the top briefly shows "Saving..." and then settles back to "Saved," confirming the change went through without you needing to do anything else.

steps.heading: Confirm your share link still works
steps.body: Because the title is just display text and not part of the form's underlying ID, changing it doesn't touch the actual share URL. Anyone who already has the link, or has it saved as a favorite, can keep using it exactly as before — they'll simply see the new name once they open it.

steps.heading: Preview how the new title reads
steps.body: Before telling people the form is ready, click Preview in the toolbar to see the form exactly as a respondent would, including how the updated title wraps and displays on both desktop and mobile widths. It's a quick sanity check that a longer replacement title isn't getting awkwardly cut off for people filling it out on a phone.

faq.question: Can I rename a form from the home dashboard grid?
faq.answer: No — the three-dot ellipsis menu on the dashboard only handles copying and moving forms. You need to open the form itself and click its title to rename it.

faq.question: Will renaming my form break the existing share link?
faq.answer: No — the title is separate from the form's underlying ID, so the backend keeps your existing share URL valid regardless of any title changes you make.

faq.question: Do I need to click a save button after renaming?
faq.answer: No — Microsoft Forms saves your updated title automatically as soon as you press Enter or click away from the text field, shown briefly by a "Saving..." indicator.

faq.question: How do I check how my new title looks to respondents?
faq.answer: Click the Preview button in the toolbar at the top of the editor to see exactly how the updated title and form render for someone filling it out.

faq.question: Where exactly is the title field in the editor?
faq.answer: It's the large header text sitting directly above your list of questions on the editor canvas — click straight on it to turn it into an editable text field.
